title: Baby Dodds at a lakefront dance, Bill Russell, later gig in New York
summary: Steiner recalls hearing the band with Baby Dodds at a park dance; Lovett met Bill Russell once and later played with Dodds in New York.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, I mentioned, yes, I mentioned that I had heard you with Baby Dodds, I'm quite certain about this, G-E-R-O-U-L-D. In a park on the edge of Lake Michigan at about 55th Street. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I think it was called Promontory Park or something of that sort. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And it was a field house or a band house or something of that sort out there in the park. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. On a weekend night, probably a Friday night, playing for a dance and some of the jazz enthusiasts at the school may have promoted it. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I don't remember the circumstances for it. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. But I would suspect that it was Cakewalking Babes with Baby Dodds either setting in for a set or maybe for a while. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Did Bill Russell ever run a session out there? Is it possible that it was Bill Russell's session?

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I don't think so. I remember I met Bill Russell once when I was with Don Ewell. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Bill Russell came to town for something or other. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I remember I met him once.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, Bill wasn't living here at that time then. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. No. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, alright. Then he wouldn't have run. Later on when he came into town he began to run some sessions.
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Oh, I do remember later I played with Baby Dodds at the Central Plaza in New York, possibly in 1950 or 51. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Was Bunk too? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. No. No, this was after Bunk left.
